column.name: name
column.description: Machine name of the business signal, e.g. pdp_impressions.

column.name: is_higher_better
column.description: Whether a HIGHER raw value is the better outcome for this signal (e.g. sales) as opposed to a lower one (e.g. days since restock, return rate). Not inferrable from the data — direction is business knowledge. Used by the normalization-curve fit suggestion to pick increasing vs. decreasing candidate shapes; does not affect the formula itself.

column.name: store_name
column.description: e.g. DE — a business-behavior metric's formula/active flag/curve shape is a store-level fact (conversion, stock, warehouse reality), not a language preference; deliberately NOT locale-scoped, unlike weight and the specificity/relevance settings, which genuinely are locale-sensitive (tokenization/decompounding). See spy_search_ranking_metric.is_higher_better for the one identity field that stays global instead of moving here — direction is a semantic property of what the metric MEANS, not a per-store fact.

column.name: formula
column.description: This store's own normalization expression mapping raw values into ]0;1]; variables: x, min, max, avg, count. The columns that once held a single global formula/isActive/shape on spy_search_ranking_metric itself were removed entirely once every part of this package migrated onto this store-scoped table (a breaking change; see CHANGELOG.md for the release that shipped it — no live installs meant no backfill migration was needed). A brand-new store gets its rows via Scope Copy's Sync Store Config action instead, then diverges per store as each is independently re-fit against its own digest.

column.name: is_active
column.description: Only active metrics are normalized and exported to the search index, for THIS store.

column.name: shape
column.description: Stable curve-family slug (e.g. atan, sigmoid, hyperbolic) for this store's own formula; NULL for a freeform/custom formula that matches no known candidate shape. Same derivation as spy_search_ranking_metric.shape had, now per store.

column.name: store_name
column.description: e.g. DE — a metric's weight in the combined ranking score is store+locale scoped; its definition (formula/isActive/isHigherBetter/shape) on spy_search_ranking_metric is not.

column.name: locale_name
column.description: e.g. de_DE.

column.name: weight
column.description: Weight of this metric in the combined ranking score, for this store+locale.

column.name: store_name
column.description: A metric's raw_value distribution is store+locale scoped (see spy_search_ranking_product_metric), so its digest must be too — a global digest would blend unrelated stores' signal distributions.

column.name: min_value
column.description: Smallest raw_value across the metric's product rows for this store+locale, at the time this digest was computed.

column.name: max_value
column.description: Largest raw_value across the metric's product rows for this store+locale, at the time this digest was computed.

column.name: median_value
column.description: The p50 percentile point — also the default fit parameter (k) for the x/(x+k) saturating candidate, the same 0.5-crossover principle relevanceSaturationPoint already uses.

column.name: sample_count
column.description: Number of raw_value rows the digest was computed from.

column.name: percentiles
column.description: The empirical CDF as a fixed-size backbone: 101 comma-separated raw_value points at percentiles 0,1,2,...,100 (ascending), i.e. percentiles[p] is the raw_value below which p% of products fall.

column.name: setting_key
column.description: Machine name of the setting, e.g. relevance_weight.

column.name: store_name
column.description: e.g. DE — Zed has no implicit current store, callers must pick explicitly.

column.name: locale_name
column.description: e.g. de_DE.

column.name: setting_key
column.description: Same machine name as spy_search_ranking_setting.setting_key, e.g. relevance_weight.

column.name: setting_value
column.description: spy_search_ranking_setting.setting_value for this key/store/locale at the time of this snapshot.

column.name: store_name
column.description: e.g. DE — a business signal like pdp_impressions is naturally store-specific (and, for some metrics, locale-specific too).

column.name: raw_value
column.description: Real-world signal value, e.g. number of PDP impressions.

column.name: normalized_value
column.description: Value in ]0;1] derived from raw_value by the metric formula; null until the normalization cron ran.

column.name: source_store_name
column.description: e.g. DE — the scope whose weights/settings are copied FROM, once immediately on lock creation and then daily by the sync cron. A scope may be the source of several active locks at once (fan-out to multiple new markets) but never simultaneously a target of any active lock.

column.name: source_locale_name
column.description: e.g. de_DE.

column.name: target_store_name
column.description: e.g. AT — the scope whose weights/settings are copied INTO. May be the target of at most one active lock at a time (unambiguous which source feeds it), and never simultaneously a source of any active lock.

column.name: is_active
column.description: False once unlocked. Rows are never deleted, only deactivated — an append-only log of lock episodes, so the active-locks page can show history. A scope's eligibility as source/target for a NEW lock is a point-in-time check against is_active=true rows only: once unlocked, a scope is fully free again for either role, there is no permanent lifetime tag.

column.name: deactivated_at
column.description: When this lock was unlocked; null while is_active is true.

column.name: fk_search_ranking_metric
column.description: Deliberately NOT a Propel foreign key (see below) — plain indexed column only.

column.name: metric_name
column.description: Denormalized: history must stay readable even if the live metric is later renamed or deleted.

column.name: store_name
column.description: Which store+locale this snapshot's weight/digest applied to — a metric's weight and digest are store+locale scoped, its formula/isActive/isHigherBetter are not, but the whole row is still recorded per (store, locale) for a simple, complete audit trail.

column.name: weight
column.description: spy_search_ranking_metric_weight.weight for this store+locale at the time of this snapshot.

column.name: formula
column.description: spy_search_ranking_metric.formula at the time of this snapshot.

column.name: min_value
column.description: The metric's digest for this store+locale at the time of this snapshot, null if no digest existed yet (e.g. a brand-new metric with no product-metric rows).

column.name: percentiles
column.description: Comma-separated 101-point percentile backbone at the time of this snapshot, same shape as spy_search_ranking_metric_digest.percentiles.

column.name: fit_r_squared
column.description: R² of `formula` (this row's) against `percentiles` (this row's) at the time of this snapshot; null if no digest existed yet to fit against.

column.name: is_change
column.description: True: this row records an actual formula/weight/isActive/isHigherBetter change (what search-ranking:randomize-style writers and manual saves both produce today). False: reserved for a future periodic check-only snapshot (no change made) — lets a drift-detection query anchor on the last REAL change rather than the last snapshot taken, so an unchanged formula's comparison baseline correctly grows (30 days, then 60, then 90, ...) instead of resetting to the most recent check every time.

column.name: change_source
column.description: SearchRankingConfig::CHANGE_SOURCE_* (Shared) — who/what produced this row: manual (a human editing the metric directly on this package's own Zed pages), or, once spryker-community/search-ranking-optimizer is installed and writing through it, auto_tune (Auto-Tune runner picked a new formula on its own), optimizer_apply (human applied an optimizer run's machine-computed weight) or checkpoint_restore (human restored a prior weight checkpoint). Defaults to manual so every row this package alone can ever produce is correctly labeled without a caller having to say so.
